{"answer":"Logistic regression is a statistical and machine‑learning technique used to model the probability of a binary outcome (e.g., yes/no, success/failure) as a function of one or more predictor variables. It assumes that the log‑odds (logit) of the outcome are a linear combination of the predictors:

\[
	ext{logit}(p) = \ln\!\left( rac{p}{1-p}ight) =  eta_0 +  eta_1x_1 + \dots +  eta_kx_k
\]

where \(p\) is the probability that the outcome equals 1. The logistic function (sigmoid) transforms this linear combination back into a probability:

\[
p =  rac{1}{1 + e^{-( eta_0 +  eta_1x_1 + \dots +  eta_kx_k)}}
\]

Parameters \( eta\) are estimated by maximizing the likelihood of observing the data (maximum likelihood estimation). Logistic regression can be extended to multinomial outcomes (multiclass classification) and to handle regularization (L1/L2) to prevent overfitting.

Typical applications include medical diagnosis (disease vs. no disease), credit scoring (default vs. no default), and many other binary decision problems."}
